independent_answer: A context switch preserves the outgoing kernel thread's saved register context so execution can later resume, and restores the incoming thread's context. In these excerpts, swtch saves ra, sp, and s0 through s11, but not caller-saved registers. A process kernel thread switches to its CPU's scheduler thread, which selects another process kernel thread and switches to it.

evidence_quotes.quote: it saves the switched-from thread’s CPU registers, and restores the previously-saved registers of the switched-to thread.
swtch saves callee-saved registers (ra,sp,s0..s11) but not caller-saved registers.

Xv6 does not directly context switch from one process’s kernel thread to another process’s kernel thread; instead, a kernel thread gives up the CPU by context-switching to that CPU’s “scheduler thread,” and the scheduler thread picks a different process’s kernel thread to run, and context-switches to that thread.

independent_answer: 按题面明确给出的范围，swtch 保存切出线程的 ra、sp、s0..s11，并恢复切入线程对应的寄存器，使线程能从原先的执行位置和栈环境继续运行；它不保存调用者保存寄存器。若允许补充通常的函数调用约定，其原因是需要跨 swtch 调用保留的调用者保存寄存器由调用方负责，而不是由 swtch 保存；题面本身没有给出这条原因。调度器线程充当本 CPU 的切换中介：进程内核线程先切换到调度器线程，由后者选择可运行的进程内核线程，再切换到该线程。不能从所给要点进一步推断其他硬件状态均不需要保存。

evidence_quotes.quote: thread memory need not saved and restored because different threads keep their data in different areas of RAM; but the CPU has only one set of registers so they must be switched (saved and restored) between threads.

The RISC-V calling convention requires that if code needs to preserve the value in a caller-saved register across a function call, the compiler must generate instructions that save the register to the stack before the function call, and restore from the stack when the function returns.

It is important to retry the complete transaction, including all logic that decides which SQL to issue and/or which values to use. Therefore, PostgreSQL does not offer an automatic retry facility, since it cannot do so with any guarantee of correctness.
In all other cases applications must not depend on results read during a transaction that later aborted; instead, they should retry the transaction until it succeeds.

evidence_quotes.quote: TCP guarantees the reliable, in-order delivery of a stream of bytes. It is a full-duplex protocol, meaning that each TCP connection supports a pair of byte streams, one flowing in each direction.
Although “byte stream” describes the service TCP offers to application processes, TCP does not, itself, transmit individual bytes over the Internet.
The packets exchanged between TCP peers in Figure 127 are called segments, since each one carries a segment of the byte stream.

This buffer holds data that arrives out of order, as well as data that is in the correct order (i.e., there are no missing bytes earlier in the stream) but that the application process has not yet had the chance to read.
